Application Materials.content:
Write your application, including references, CV, transcripts, and personal statement.
- **References:** You must supply **one academic or professional reference**; your referee can know you on either an academic or professional level. Once you have paid your application fee, Warwick will email your referee inviting them to submit a reference online. It is your responsibility to ensure that your reference has been submitted. References submitted by email will not be acceptable.
- **CV:** You are required to submit a CV as part of the application process. Your CV should contain your educational background, employment history, any volunteering experience, and any extra-curricular activities, hobbies and interests.
- **Transcripts:** You must upload a final or interim transcript for your undergraduate bachelor’s degree. Your transcripts must show the modules you have taken for each year, including the first year, and the marks you have gained to date. Please also upload a list of your final year modules as a **PDF or Word document**. If your transcript is not printed in English, please also include a translation.
- **Personal Statement:** Key areas to cover include: why you have selected this course and your motivating factors; how you see the course benefitting your career plans; and what you will contribute to your cohort. Warwick says this is your opportunity to share achievements and ambitions and advises avoiding repeating information from your CV.
- **Supporting documents:** Following submission of your application and payment of your application fee, the Postgraduate Admissions team will send an email with a link to access the upload facility. Documents cannot be submitted via email and applicants should not post hard copy documents at this time. If made an offer, applicants will then be asked to supply original documents.
- **Translations:** All transcripts from higher learning must be officially translated. A valid translation must have an original stamp from an official translation company and be attached to the original document.
- You only need to upload one set of supplementary documents with each application, but Warwick recommends tailoring each Personal Statement specifically for every course applied to.

Interview Requirements.content: At WBS, there are **no interviews for MSc courses**. Instead, all decisions are made based on the application you submit. Your undergraduate transcript will be reviewed in depth along with your CV and personal statement.

Application Deadlines.content:
Our current application deadline is **2 August 2026**, however applications may close earlier if all places on a course are filled prior to the deadline. We advise our international candidates to apply as early as possible to ensure sufficient time to process visa applications.
- Application Deadline: **2 August 2026**
- Start Date: **September 2026**

Academic Requirements.content:
- You must have, or be expecting to obtain, **at least a 2.1 degree at Undergraduate level from a UK university or overseas equivalent**.
- The course requires **strong numeracy and IT statistical ability**.
- Applications are considered from a wide range of degrees such as **economics, business, engineering, psychology, geography, sociology, and politics**.
- When assessing your academic record, Warwick Business School takes into account your **grade average** and the **position of the institution** where you studied your qualification.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
If English is not your first language, you must meet a minimum overall standard in a recognised test of English. You must show a good balance across all sections of the test and it must have been taken within **two years of starting the course**. Certificates are required as evidence.
- **IELTS (Academic, UKVI or Online): 7.0 overall**, with a maximum of two language components at lowest level 6.0/6.5 and the rest at 7.0 or above. One skill retakes are not accepted; the test must be taken in one sitting.
- **CPE: 190 overall**; 2 x 170, 2 x 190.
- **CAE: 190 overall**; 2 x 170, 2 x 190.
- **TOEFL: 5**; minimum language components L4.5, R4.5, W4.5, S4.5.
- **Trinity ISE III:** Merit, Merit, Pass, Pass in four components.
- **Trinity ISE IV:** Pass, Pass, Pass, Pass in four components.
- **Duolingo: Band B: 130**, with at least 110 in two components and 130 in two components.
If you are a non-native speaker of English but have been educated entirely in English for your degree, and completed this within the last two years, this may satisfy the University of your language skills. [See more details on English Language Requirements on the University's website](http://www2.warwick.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/apply/english/).

Program Overview.content:
**MSc Business Analytics & Artificial Intelligence** teaches students how to gain insights from large data sets using Artificial Intelligence (AI), statistical methods, optimisation and machine learning, and apply them to business challenges. The course covers cutting-edge and industry-standard analytical techniques, including visualisation in Tableau, machine learning, statistics and optimisation, and provides cross-disciplinary training in business models, quantitative methods and data science.
- Ranked 3rd in the UK and 17th in the world in the QS University Rankings 2025.
- MSc Business Analytics, now MSc Business Analytics & Artificial Intelligence, is ranked 3rd in the UK and 13th in the world in the QS Business Masters Rankings 2026.
- Students learn how to translate a variety of data into business value through cutting-edge techniques, cover analytics modules from data engineering to applied statistics aligned with industry trends, and continue developing programming skills in SQL, R, and Python, as well as the use of AI tools.
- Students can conduct an [external consultancy project](https://www.wbs.ac.uk/courses/masters/business-analytics-artificial-intelligence/structure/?tab=dissertation-or-business-in-practice) with a real client, undertake [individual academic research](https://www.wbs.ac.uk/courses/masters/business-analytics-artificial-intelligence/structure/?tab=dissertation-or-business-in-practice), or put their learnings into practice with the applied [Business in Practice](https://www.wbs.ac.uk/courses/masters/business-analytics-artificial-intelligence/structure/?tab=dissertation-or-business-in-practice) module.
- Duration: 1 year; Location: Warwick Campus; Format: Full-time; Start Date: September 2026.
- Formerly MSc Business Analytics, this course has been reviewed and relaunched for 2026 entry.
- The dedicated [MSc CareersPlus & Employer Relations](https://www.wbs.ac.uk/courses/masters/careers/) team provides personalised support throughout the journey. Graduates have recently secured roles including AI Analyst, Data Consultant and Market Strategy Lead at employers such as Accenture, EY and KPMG.
- The graduating Class of 2025 averaged a salary of $71,541 (converted for PPP) within six months of completion. This data reflects those that participated in the [MSc Employment Report](https://online.flippingbook.com/view/763598704/) survey, which averaged a 72% response rate overall; this cohort studied the 'MSc Business Analytics' version of this course, which has since been reviewed and relaunched for 2026 entry.
- Warwick Business School is accredited by [AACSB](https://eur01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.aacsb.edu%2F&data=05%7C02%7CFrances.Hannon%40wbs.ac.uk%7Cb677ac2e2de94c09798c08dd160bf953%7C09bacfbd47ef446592653546f2eaf6bc%7C0%7C0%7C638690962864845291%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=VT1zWN4XATEGflMdOLd30pk1mmNp1alRbuphI3EEC2w%3D&reserved=0), [AMBA](https://eur01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.associationofmbas.com%2F&data=05%7C02%7CFrances.Hannon%40wbs.ac.uk%7Cb677ac2e2de94c09798c08dd160bf953%7C09bacfbd47ef446592653546f2eaf6bc%7C0%7C0%7C638690962864874627%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=i0896JksgKYDMPMYR%2BpLdCIuOz%2FHrZrgLyQSj3f5jRA%3D&reserved=0) and [EQUIS](https://eur01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.efmdglobal.org%2Faccreditations-assessments%2Fbusiness-schools%2Fequis%2F&data=05%7C02%7CFrances.Hannon%40wbs.ac.uk%7Cb677ac2e2de94c09798c08dd160bf953%7C09bacfbd47ef446592653546f2eaf6bc%7C0%7C0%7C638690962864893377%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=nu3y6VlY%2B31LbdV0JkD8LItR4ZYIHTj4NxloZiz0CsM%3D&reserved=0), and holds [gold level Athena Swan](https://eur01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wbs.ac.uk%2Fabout%2Fequality-diversity-and-inclusion%2Fathena-swan%2F&data=05%7C02%7CFrances.Hannon%40wbs.ac.uk%7Cb677ac2e2de94c09798c08dd160bf953%7C09bacfbd47ef446592653546f2eaf6bc%7C0%7C0%7C638690962864913602%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=BycHkzvNKHIELjLUN5kVqTHnDVt9fy03WSP3e8TxF1U%3D&reserved=0) status.

Curriculum.content:
Over three terms you will complete four core modules, alongside four modules from one of the new specialisms: Artificial Intelligence; Predictive and Prescriptive Analytics; Management Analytics; and Marketing Analytics & Technology. Assessment will vary between group presentations, peer assessments, individual assignments and examinations.
Your studies will be completed by one of the following routes:
- One elective + Research Paper
- Two electives + Self-sourced Internship
- Two electives + Business in Practice
- Two electives + Analytics Portfolio.
You will develop your programming skills in Python, SQL and R, and gain guidance in obtaining optional certifications such as Associate Certified Analytics Professional. You will be given access to a wide-range of additional analytics and data science online courses, and gain exposure to industry-standard software such as Tableau, PyTorch and Large Language Models.
Core modules include:
- Analytics Engineering, AI and Visualisation: theoretical and practical exposure to modern data workflows in business analytics and AI, covering data extraction through to product deployment in the form of business dashboards.
- Analytics in Practice: how to structure and conduct an end-to-end analytics/data science project including data engineering, modelling using machine learning methods, visualisation and communicating results to the end-user.
- Applied Analytics Projects: an opportunity to apply the techniques and methodologies taught on the course to real-world settings, including project management for analytical interventions, ethics and risks in analytics projects, and structuring analytics in the business model of the organisation.
- Business Statistics: a foundation in the analysis and presentation of quantitative data and the basic elements of statistics that are the foundation of analytics and business analysis.
Specialisms:
- Artificial Intelligence: Advanced Data Analysis; Algorithms and Optimisation in Software Applications; Deep Learning and AI Engineering; Generative AI and AI Applications.
- Management Analytics: Developing an Analytics Capability; Financial Analytics; Prescriptive Analytics and Optimisation; Supply Chain Analytics.
- Marketing Analytics and Technology: Algorithms and Optimisation in Software Applications; Developing an Analytics Capability; Generative AI and AI Applications; Marketing and Digital Analytics.
- Predictive and Prescriptive Analytics: Advanced Analytics: Models and Applications; Advanced Data Analysis; Deep Learning and AI Engineering; Prescriptive Analytics and Optimisation.
Indicative optional modules may vary year-on-year and include: AI and Moral Decision-Making in Business; Business, International Finance & Economics; Case Studies in Data Science & Economics; Consumer Behaviour; Digital Business Services; Digital Marketing Technology and Management; Digital Strategy and Agile Transformation; Entrepreneurship and Business Venturing; FinTech for Consumer Financial Services; Forecasting; International Business; Leading for Innovation; Pricing Analytics; Strategic Human Resource Management. Key: * Analytics Portfolio, Business in Practice and Internship routes only.
Pathways:
- Analytics Portfolio: structure analytics projects, perform hands-on analysis of data, interpret results in the context of the business domain, and develop a visual portfolio of your work.
- Business in Practice: an alternative to the traditional route, simulating real-life business challenges; after the simulation you will complete an Individual Reflection and a Business Analysis.
- Self-sourced Internship: opportunity to self-source a summer internship to apply theoretical learnings to a real-world industry setting.
- Research Paper: conduct academic research on a topic critical to effective decision-making in organisations, under the guidance and supervision of academics.
Your course will be taught through a mix of face-to-face and online learning, utilising the format most suitable to the content. Your learning will be assessed by a mix of exams, individual assessments, group work, project work, and tests. The online learning platform my.wbs will host teaching materials, key information, and the online classroom wbsLive.
Duration: **1 year**. Location: **Warwick Campus**. Format: **Full-time**.

Cost of Attendance.content:
Monthly living costs for a student at Warwick University include:
- Groceries: **£153**
- Socialising (including eating out/takeaway): **£129**
- Holidays & Events: **£29**
- Transport: **£53**
- Clothes & Shopping: **£35**
- Phone: **£15**
- Health & Wellbeing: **£28**
- Laundry: **£5.50 per load**
According to [Save the Students' Living Cost Survey 2025](https://www.savethestudent.org/money/student-budgeting/what-do-students-spend-their-money-on.html), Warwick students spend on average **£49** per month on bills. A full day of parking on campus costs **£8.50** from **1st September 2025**. Health costs students may face include NHS prescriptions at **£9.90 per item**. If you live on campus, laundry costs approximately **£5.50 per average load (wash and dry)** at the campus laundrette.

Financial Aid.content:
We have £1.5 million+ of [WBS scholarships](https://www.wbs.ac.uk/courses/masters/scholarships/) available for students applying to study on our MSc postgraduate courses. Scholarships awards range from 10% of your tuition fee to a maximum of 50% for exceptional candidates. They are highly competitive and awarded on an ongoing basis, so applicants are strongly encouraged to apply early.
- **The OR Society Scholarships**: Each year The OR Society offers two master's degree scholarships of up to £10,000 towards tuition fees for UK students who demonstrate academic ability but require funding to continue their studies and fulfil their potential in making a future contribution to Operational Research. [Discover more on The OR Society website.](https://www.theorsociety.com/what-we-do/awards-medals-and-scholarships/masters-scholarship/)
- **High Potential Scholarship**: For those who stand out academically, challenge the norm, and have gone beyond their course to delve deeper into extra-curricular activities, volunteering work, or student societies.
- **Warwick Undergraduate Scholarship**: Warwick students will be awarded with an automatic 30% scholarship (with 10% of this scholarship coming from the Warwick Alumni Discount Scheme). You will also be considered for our other scholarships, which could discount up to a further 20%.
- **Alumni Scholarship**: All alumni from the University of Warwick who are accepted onto a postgraduate Master's receive a minimum 25% scholarship, and up to an additional 25% for exceptional academic and/or extra-curricular achievements.
- **UK and Commonwealth Scholarship**: For outstanding individuals across the UK and Commonwealth to encourage geographical diversity.
- **International/EU Scholarship**: Available on a competitive basis for exceptional talent living outside of the UK or the Commonwealth.
- [Country-specific partnerships & scholarships](https://warwick.ac.uk/study/international/admissions/finance/scholarships "COUNTRY-SPECIFIC PARTNERSHIPS & SCHOLARSHIPS")
- [Warwick and External Scholarships](https://warwick.ac.uk/study/scholarships-and-bursaries/ "Warwick and External Scholarships")
- [More about fees and funding](https://warwick.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/funding/funding-routes "More about fees and funding")
If you have a disability, including a mental-health condition or specific learning difficulty, such as dyslexia or dyspraxia, you might be able to get Disabled Students’ Allowance (DSAs). DSAs don’t have to be paid back. Postgraduate students can apply for DSAs even if they aren’t eligible for a Postgraduate Loan.

Multiple Applications.content: You may apply for as many courses as you wish, however you will need to complete a new application form for each course and an application assessment fee is payable for each taught application. You can apply to each course only once during an admissions cycle. If a duplicate application is made it will be deleted.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
Some departments do allow applicants to defer their offer (not application) to a later date or by **one academic year**.
- If your request to defer your offer is approved by your department, the Admissions Service may ask you to meet some conditions again, for example if your English language certificate is no longer valid.
- Departments usually only allow applicants to defer once.
- If a request to change a start date or defer your studies is approved, **the central admissions team will review your record and may be required to add conditions back into your offer**.
- **Changing your start date or deferring will in many cases, result is fee increases**. Details regarding fees will be included on your new offer letter.
- **In some cases, in order for the admissions team to amend your record and change your start dates, we will have to request that the enrolment team withdraw your record initially**.
- **If you have began the CAS process before completing this form, please note that you may incur extra costs if you choose to proceed with changing your start date or deferring**. By completing this form, you are confirming that you wish for Warwick to withdraw your CAS.
- [Please complete the form to request to defer your offer.](https://warwick.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/apply/pgadmissions/offerholders/respond/defer/request_deferral)

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
If your application is approved, the University will make an official offer of a place on the course. There is normally a time limit to accept this. **Offers may be conditional on you meeting academic, language, or other requirements.** Once you have met your conditions, the offer will automatically be made unconditional.
You can apply before you have completed your degree. You will need to supply interim transcripts of your marks and modules to date with your application. You can also apply before you have received your language score. You should put the date of your English test on your application form and you can send in your score later. In both cases, **if an offer is made it will most likely be conditional and dependent on you achieving the required grade/score for admission.**
